To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the meaning of facial expression is not universal but depends on the communicator's physical attractiveness, and (b) attractive people are more likely to be judged positively, but this advantage is reduced when they are not smiling.

(1) both facial expression and physical attractiveness had a positive main-effect on judgments, and (2) there was a significant, and nonobvious, interaction between facial expression and physical appearance on judgments of self confidence and responsibility.
(1) physical attractiveness is a powerful cue in the interpretation of nonverbal cues and (2) the meaning of non- verbal cues depends on the physical attractiveness and the sex of the communicator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of physical attractiveness in the interpretation of facial expression cues.
the role of physical attractiveness in the interpretation of facial expression cues.
the question of how the meaning of non verbal signals depends on the physical attractiveness (or lack of attractiveness) of the communicator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meaning of a facial expression is not only determined by the expression itself but also by the physical attractiveness of its communicator.
the meaning of non verbal cues does depend on the physical characteristics of the communicator.

the physical attractiveness of a communicator has a positive impact on the interpretation of facial expression cues and that the meaning of facial expression cues is not the same for all communicators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the meaning of facial expression depends on the physical attractiveness (or unattractiveness) of the person expressing it.
the meaning of non-verbal cues depends on the physical attractiveness and sex of the communicator.
physical attractiveness and facial expressions interact in complex ways to influence judgments of others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical attractiveness can be an important cue to nonverbal behavior, and that the meaning of non-verbal behavior can be affected by the physical attractiveness of a communicator.

facial expressions are not interpreted in the same way when they are displayed by attractive and unattractive individuals, and that the same facial expression may be interpreted as conveying very different meanings when displayed by different communicators.
people tend to interpret facial expression cues in ways that are congruent with their expectations about the communicator’s physical attractiveness.
